                                         ergy between visual and linguistic modalities through large        fixed number of frames are evenly selected from the video
                                         language models, enabling them to capture complex re-              [1, 14, 38]. Although simple and efficient, this approach of-
                                         lationships and contextual cues over time. They have               ten fails in complex real-world scenarios because it assumes
                                         demonstrated remarkable advancements in tasks such as              that all frames contribute equally to content understanding,
                                         video captioning [4, 33, 37] and video question answer-            which may hold true for short, query-trimmed videos but
                                         ing [12, 21, 23]. However, large VLMs face significant             not for long, unedited ones. For example, instructional or
                                         challenges in processing long videos containing thousands          surveillance videos usually contain lengthy segments irrel-
                                         of frames due to the sheer volume of video tokens. For             evant to the given query. Sampling frames from these seg-

improved by selecting query-related frames. (b) Top-K selection often yields redundant frames with limited diversity. (c) Watershed
grouping may overlook broader temporal context. (d) Inverse transform sampling can prioritize relevant frames while preserving selec-
tion diversity, achieving stronger performance on benchmarks, particularly for videos with noisy backgrounds.

used. Our training-free approach BOLT enables off-the-shelf VLM LLaVA-OneVision to focus on query-related frames, thereby boosting
the VQA performance in various settings. It also outperforms other large VLMs in the literature with comparable model scales.

B. Analysis of Inference Cost
We also evaluate the inference cost of our training-free ap-
proach. Our method consists of three main steps: CLIP-
based frame feature encoding, inverse transform sampling,                                          004-1.png
and VLM inference. In terms of memory usage, our ap-                                               006-2.png
proach requires nearly the same GPU memory as the base-
line method that uses uniform sampling. In terms of infer-
ence time, as shown in Table 11, the total inference time
per sample increases by approximately 90%, primarily due
to the CLIP feature encoding step. In contrast, the inverse
transform sampling itself is highly efficient. Although our
method introduces some additional inference time, it re-                Figure 4. When visual-query similarity scores remain similar
mains acceptable considering that no training or fine-tuning            across the video, inverse transform sampling simplifies to uni-
is required.                                                            form sampling.


                                                                   11
                        004-1.png
                        006-2.png




          Figure 5. Additional visualization results.


maintain important contextual information required for ac-
curate video understanding.
   In Figure 4, we present an example where the visual-
query similarity scores remain relatively similar through-
out the video. In such cases, the cumulative distribution
function becomes approximately linear, causing the final se-
lected frames to approximate uniform sampling. This indi-
cates that most clips in the video may contribute equally to
answering the question.
